result.title: Real-Time On-Drone Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection for Wilderness Search and Rescue
result.summary: Wilderness search-and-rescue (WSAR) teams use uncrewed aerial systems (UASs) to survey terrain for indicators of missing persons that are rare, blend into the background, or lack thermal signatures. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) provides rich spectral information, but its high data volume challenges real-time on-drone processing. We present SABL, an edge-computing pipeline for on-drone Spectral Anomaly-Based Localization. SABL integrates hyperspectral streaming with exponentially moving Reed-Xiaoli (ERX) anomaly detection and DBSCAN spatial filtering to group pixel-level anomalies into candidate search regions. SABL is evaluated on data collected during a 10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue (QSAR) in remote Alaska. It processes hyperspectral scanlines at 5.67-5.73 ms per line, meeting the camera's 10-ms acquisition interval; DBSCAN requires only 6.5-12.5 ms per 100-line update for filtering. SABL achieves approximately 56% and 99% object-level precision on QSAR-selected search indicators across two scenes, with corresponding recall of 55% and 29%, providing significant background filtering while identifying difficult-to-see anomalous search indicators.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SABL，一套部署在无人机上的边缘计算流水线，用指数滑动 Reed-Xiaoli 异常检测结合 DBSCAN 空间聚类，从高光谱流数据中实时圈定野外搜救候选区域。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属遥感高光谱异常检测的工程部署，采用固定流程的传统统计方法与聚类，不涉及多模态模型的内部表示、latent 推理状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
